passages.text: Then I was given a measuring rod like a staff and was told, “Go and measure the temple of God and the altar, and count the number of worshipers there.
passages.sermon:
I received a measuring rod.
The rod was like a staff.
Someone spoke to me.
They told me to get up.
They told me to measure the temple of God.
They told me to measure the altar.
They told me to count the people worshiping in the temple.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐδόθη μοι κάλαμος ὅμοιος ῥάβδῳ λέγων Ἔγειρε καὶ μέτρησον τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: But exclude the courtyard outside the temple. Do not measure it, because it has been given over to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for 42 months.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to John in a vision.
God told John to leave out the courtyard outside the temple.
God told John not to measure the courtyard.
God said the courtyard belongs to the nations.
The nations will trample the holy city.
They will trample it for forty-two months.
passages.original: καὶ τὴν αὐλὴν τὴν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ναοῦ ἔκβαλε ἔξωθεν καὶ μὴ αὐτὴν μετρήσῃς ὅτι ἐδόθη τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν πατήσουσιν μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ δύο

passages.text: And I will empower my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth.”
passages.sermon:
God will give power to His two witnesses.
These two witnesses will speak God’s message.
They will prophesy for 1,260 days.
They will wear sackcloth.
passages.original: καὶ δώσω τοῖς δυσὶν μάρτυσίν μου καὶ προφητεύσουσιν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα περιβεβλημένοι σάκκους

passages.text: These witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses stand before the Lord of the earth.
They are like two olive trees.
They are like two lampstands.
They remain in the presence of the Lord.
passages.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι καὶ αἱ δύο λυχνίαι αἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἑστῶτες

passages.text: If anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouths and devours their enemies. In this way, anyone who wants to harm them must be killed.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses stand before the Lord of the earth.
If anyone wants to harm the two witnesses, fire comes out of their mouths.
This fire destroys their enemies.
Anyone who tries to harm the two witnesses must be killed in this way.
passages.original: καὶ εἴ τις αὐτοὺς θέλει ἀδικῆσαι πῦρ ἐκπορεύεται ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτῶν καὶ κατεσθίει τοὺς ἐχθροὺς αὐτῶν καὶ εἴ τις θελήσῃ αὐτοὺς ἀδικῆσαι οὕτως δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀποκτανθῆναι

passages.text: These witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy, and power to turn the waters into blood and to strike the earth with every kind of plague as often as they wish.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses stand before the Lord of the earth.
They have great power from God.
They can shut the sky.
No rain will fall during the days when they prophesy.
They have power over the waters.
They can turn the waters into blood.
They can strike the earth with every kind of plague.
They can do this as often as they wish.
passages.original: οὗτοι ἔχουσιν τὴν ἐξουσίαν κλεῖσαι τὸν οὐρανόν ἵνα μὴ ὑετὸς βρέχῃ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς προφητείας αὐτῶν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσιν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων στρέφειν αὐτὰ εἰς αἷμα καὶ πατάξαι τὴν γῆν ἐν πάσῃ πληγῇ ὁσάκις ἐὰν θελήσωσιν

passages.text: When the two witnesses have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them, and will overpower and kill them.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses speak for God.
They finish giving their testimony.
A beast rises from the Abyss.
This beast fights against the two witnesses.
The beast defeats them.
The beast kills them.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν τελέσωσιν τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτῶν τὸ θηρίον τὸ ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου ποιήσει μετ’ αὐτῶν πόλεμον καὶ νικήσει αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀποκτενεῖ αὐτούς

passages.text: Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city—figuratively called Sodom and Egypt—where their Lord was also crucified.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses will die.
Their bodies will lie in the street.
This street is in the great city.
People call this city Sodom and Egypt in a spiritual sense.
Their Lord was crucified in this city.
passages.original: καὶ τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τῆς πλατείας τῆς πόλεως τῆς μεγάλης ἥτις καλεῖται πνευματικῶς Σόδομα καὶ Αἴγυπτος ὅπου καὶ ὁ Κύριος αὐτῶν ἐσταυρώθη

passages.text: For three and a half days all peoples and tribes and tongues and nations will view their bodies and will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.
passages.sermon:
All peoples see the bodies of the two witnesses.
All tribes see their bodies.
All languages see their bodies.
All nations see their bodies.
They look at the bodies for three and a half days.
They do not allow the bodies to be placed in a tomb.
passages.original: καὶ βλέπουσιν ἐκ τῶν λαῶν καὶ φυλῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν καὶ ἐθνῶν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἡμέρας τρεῖς καὶ ἥμισυ καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀφίουσιν τεθῆναι εἰς μνῆμα

passages.text: And those who dwell on the earth will gloat over them, and will celebrate and send one another gifts, because these two prophets had tormented them.
passages.sermon:
The people who live on the earth will rejoice over the two prophets.
They will feel glad because of the prophets’ death.
They will celebrate together.
They will send gifts to each other.
These two prophets had caused trouble for those who live on the earth.
The people celebrate because the prophets had tormented them.
passages.original: καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς χαίρουσιν ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ εὐφραίνονται καὶ δῶρα πέμψουσιν ἀλλήλοις ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ δύο προφῆται ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: But after the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses lay dead for three and a half days.
God gave them the breath of life.
The two witnesses stood up on their feet.
Everyone who saw them became very afraid.
passages.original: Καὶ μετὰ τὰς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ ἥμισυ πνεῦμα ζωῆς ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσῆλθεν ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἔστησαν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν καὶ φόβος μέγας ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τοὺς θεωροῦντας αὐτούς

passages.text: And the witnesses heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Come up here.” And they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them.
passages.sermon:
The two witnesses heard a loud voice.
The voice came from heaven.
The voice spoke to the witnesses.
The voice said, “Come up here.”
The two witnesses went up to heaven.
They went up in a cloud.
Their enemies watched them go up.
passages.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης αὐτοῖς Ἀνάβατε ὧδε καὶ ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐθεώρησαν αὐτοὺς οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν

passages.text: And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city collapsed. Seven thousand were killed in the quake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
passages.sermon:
At that hour, a great earthquake happened.
A tenth of the city fell.
The earthquake killed seven thousand people.
The rest became afraid.
They gave glory to the God of heaven.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐγένετο σεισμὸς μέγας καὶ τὸ δέκατον τῆς πόλεως ἔπεσεν καὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῷ σεισμῷ ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων χιλιάδες ἑπτά καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἔμφοβοι ἐγένοντο καὶ ἔδωκαν δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: The second woe has passed. Behold, the third woe is coming shortly.
passages.sermon: The second woe has ended.\r\nThe third woe is coming soon.
passages.original: Ἡ Οὐαὶ ἡ δευτέρα ἀπῆλθεν ἰδοὺ ἡ Οὐαὶ ἡ τρίτη ἔρχεται ταχύ

passages.text: Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.”
passages.sermon:
The seventh angel sounded his trumpet.
Loud voices spoke in heaven.
They said, “The kingdom of the world now belongs to our Lord and to His Christ.
Our Lord and His Christ will reign forever and ever.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν καὶ ἐγένοντο φωναὶ μεγάλαι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγοντες Ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ βασιλεύσει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων

passages.text: And the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God, saying: “We give thanks to You, O Lord God Almighty, the One who is and who was, because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.
passages.sermon:
Twenty-four elders sit on thrones before God.
These elders fell on their faces.
They worshiped God.
They said, “We give thanks to You, Lord God Almighty.
You are the One who is.
You are the One who was.
You have taken Your great power.
You have begun to reign.”
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι οἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καθήμενοι ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους αὐτῶν ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ λέγοντες Εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι Κύριε ὁ Θεός ὁ Παντοκράτωρ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν ὅτι εἴληφας τὴν δύναμίν σου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐβασίλευσας

passages.text: The nations were enraged, and Your wrath has come. The time has come to judge the dead and to reward Your servants the prophets, as well as the saints and those who fear Your name, both small and great— and to destroy those who destroy the earth.”
passages.sermon:
The nations became angry.
God’s wrath arrived.
The time came to judge the dead.
The time came to reward God’s servants.
God’s servants include the prophets.
God’s servants include the saints.
God’s servants include all who fear God’s name.
These people are both small and great.
The time also came to destroy those who destroy the earth.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ὠργίσθησαν καὶ ἦλθεν ἡ ὀργή σου καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι καὶ δοῦναι τὸν μισθὸν τοῖς δούλοις σου τοῖς προφήταις καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά σου τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ διαφθεῖραι τοὺς διαφθείροντας τὴν γῆν

passages.text: Then the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple. And there were flashes of lightning, and rumblings, and peals of thunder, and an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.
passages.sermon:
God has a temple in heaven.
The temple in heaven opened.
God’s ark of the covenant appeared inside His temple.
Flashes of lightning happened.
There were loud sounds.
Thunder sounded.
The ground shook with an earthquake.
A great hailstorm fell.
passages.original: Καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταὶ καὶ σεισμὸς καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη
